ai.description: *Hydrophis curtus* reaches 1.5m. It has a stout body with grey to yellow-brown bands and a pale belly. Key features include a short, blunt head and a distinctively keeled, spine-like ventral scale row.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Hydrophis curtus* is best identified by its distinctively short, stout body and a series of prominent, sharp spines along the ventral scales, which are unique among Indian sea snakes.
ai.habitat: *Hydrophis curtus* inhabits shallow coastal waters, estuaries, and mangrove ecosystems across the Indian subcontinent, typically remaining in depths of less than 30 meters.
ai.behavior: The spine-bellied sea snake is primarily nocturnal, actively hunting for bottom-dwelling gobies and other small fish in shallow coastal waters under the cover of darkness.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Hydrophis curtus* is ovoviviparous, giving birth to live young. In India, they typically produce litters of 3–16 offspring, with breeding occurring throughout the year.
ai.distributionRemarks: The Spine-bellied Sea Snake inhabits coastal waters across the Indian subcontinent, ranging from the Arabian Sea to the Bay of Bengal at sea level.
